Status Detail.value: On October 15, 2026, the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin granted a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity for Red Oak Ridge, up to 1,210 MW at the proposed site in the Town of Paris, Kenosha County, with standard conditions. Staff were directed to draft the written order, which was not yet posted as of November 17, 2026.
Status Detail.note:
This is the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin decision on the Red Oak Ridge Energy Center, docket 9837-CE-100.

Decision:
- Open the minutes of the October 15, 2026 open meeting at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=615912 and find the entry headed 9837-CE-100, on pages 7 and 8. It says 'The Commission granted a CPCN for the proposed project, with conditions.' CPCN means Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity.
- The same entry says the Commission 'directed the Division of Energy Regulation and Analysis to draft an order consistent with its discussion.' The minutes name three commissioners present, Chairperson Strand, Commissioner Nieto and Commissioner Hawkins. They do not record a vote count.

Conditions:
- Open the final decision matrix dated October 6, 2026 at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=614384 and go to Issue 7, the standard conditions. Condition a says the applicant may build at 'an installed capacity of no greater than 1,210 MW alternating current'.

Written order:
- The Commission's filing list for the docket, harvested on November 17, 2026, shows no written final decision yet. The written order should be added to Status Detail when it is posted.

Capacity (MW).note:
The project application for docket 9837-CE-100 gives 242 MW for each gas turbine generator, so the capacity stays at 242 MW.

Capacity:
- Open the public copy of the application at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=572462 and search for section 1.1.6, 'Identify each proposed generating unit'. It says 'Each gas turbine generator ("GTG") will have an individual electrical generating capacity of approximately 242 MW, for a total installed capacity of approximately 1,210 MW.'
- The same section says the most that can be delivered to the grid is 1,186 MW, or about 237 MW per unit. That is a delivery limit set by the grid connection, not the equipment size. We record the 242 MW installed figure.
- The Commission's decision matrix at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=614384 and its minutes at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=615912 both name 1,210 MW.

Equipment Manufacturer/Model.note:
The application confirms the turbine model.

Model:
- Open https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=572462 and search for section 1.1.6. It says 'The Facility will include five GE 7F.05 gas turbines and H35 hydrogen-cooled generators.'
- The air permit application to the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources at https://apps.dnr.wi.gov/warp_ext/AM_DownloadObject.aspx?id=1252907 says in its introduction 'The Project includes five proposed General Electric (GE) model 7F.05 combustion turbines'. This is a second filing by the same company, so it is not an independent source.
- A We Energies filing names a different model. See the question on capacity and model for this plant.

Turbine/Engine Technology.note:
The application describes a simple-cycle plant.

Technology:
- Open https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=572462 and search for the Project Description. It calls the plant 'a natural gas-fired simple-cycle combustion turbine-based large electric generating facility'. A simple-cycle plant with frame turbines is recorded as gas turbine.

Fuel.note:
The application says the plant burns natural gas only.

Fuel:
- Open https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=572462 and search for section 1.1.6. It says 'The Facility will be fueled by natural gas and will not include backup fuel capability.'

Backup Power.note:
The application shows this is a grid power plant with no backup fuel, so Backup Power stays no.

Backup Power:
- Open https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=572462 and search for section 1.1.6. It says 'The Facility will be fueled by natural gas and will not include backup fuel capability.'
- The same application says the plant includes 'a standby backup generator' that gives 'auto-start and backup power to essential systems' on a loss of power. That is a station service engine, not a backup fleet for a customer, so it does not make the units backup power.
- The turbines are meant for 'periods of peak electrical demand', so they supply routine power to the grid. No source says they serve as backup for a data center.

units.notes: The status stays pre-construction. The Commission granted the certificate on October 15, 2026 but no start of construction was found, and a certificate only allows construction. Start year 2030 is consistent with the We Energies application at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=568295, which says full commercial operation by June 30, 2030, so it was left alone. The project is moving, so Latest Activity was left alone. No operator was named in any document. Number of engines and capacity per engine are not filled because these are frame turbines.

qa.question: Which EIA generator ids belong to the five Red Oak Ridge units?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 lists five generators at plant 70453, named CT4, CT5, RDOR1, RDOR2 and RDOR3, each 242 MW and planned for December 2029. CT4 and CT5 are marked as pending regulatory approval and not under construction, and the other three as planned with approvals not yet started.
qa.recommendation: Type EIA plant 70453 into Other IDs for the plant. Map the five generators to units 1 to 5 in order, since the units are identical, and add each generator id to Other IDs for its unit.
qa.note:
Open the EIA-860M workbook at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx, sheet Planned, and filter Plant ID 70453. Rows list Entity Name 'Invenergy Services LLC' and Plant Name 'Red Oak Ridge Energy Center LLC'. Technology reads 'Natural Gas Fired Combustion Turbine' and Planned Operation Year reads 2029. No document found ties a particular generator id to a particular GEM unit. EIA shows a planned operating year of 2029, while GEM shows a start year of 2030.

The exact wording in the table is 'Regulatory approvals pending. Not under construction' for CT4 and CT5, and 'Planned for installation, but regulatory approvals not initiated' for the other three.

qa.question: Should capacity stay 242 MW per unit given a We Energies filing that says 1,125 MW total?
qa.finding: The project application and the Commission decision use five GE 7F.05 turbines at 242 MW each, 1,210 MW total. The We Energies purchase application says 'up to 1,125 MW (nameplate capacity) using five GE 7E.05 gas turbines', which is 225 MW each.
qa.recommendation: Leave capacity at 242 MW and the model at 7F.05 for now. Ask the project manager to check whether We Energies has received a changed turbine plan, and revisit when the written Commission order is posted.
qa.note: Open the We Energies application filed on November 20, 2025 at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=568295 and read the first page of the introduction. It says 'a high quality, natural gas- fueled 1,125 MW (nameplate capacity) simple-cycle combustion turbine'. Page 2 repeats it with 'five GE 7E.05 gas turbines'. The developer's own application at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=572462, section 1.1.6, says 'five GE 7F.05 gas turbines' at about 242 MW each. The Commission minutes at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=615912 and decision matrix at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=614384 both name 1,210 MW. The 1,186 MW figure on the Commission case page is the grid delivery limit in the application. The We Energies document is the older record of the purchase deal, and the gap may simply be an old or incorrect model name.

qa.question: Should We Energies be added as the owner, or noted as a pending buyer?
qa.finding: Wisconsin Electric Power Company, doing business as We Energies, has applied to buy 100 percent of the project, docket 6630-BS-104. The Commission has not approved it and no sale has closed.
qa.recommendation: Keep Red Oak Ridge Energy Center LLC as the owner. Add a line at the top of Notes about the pending sale and put it on the possible updates sheet.
qa.note: Open the application at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=568295 and read the first page. It says the company applies 'to acquire the Red Oak Ridge Energy Center'. The company's letter of November 12, 2026 at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=618277 says the cost estimate rose from $1,769,801,000 to $2,311,427,000, that the application is still pending, and that '100% of ROREC Project is being subscribed to by the VLC', meaning a very large customer. Its name is not given in the public record. No source says the plant serves one site, so the captive fields stay blank.

qa.question: Is the existing point and the Somers city value right for the approved site?
qa.finding: The approved site is the Proposed Site, about 25 acres of farm field in Section 13, Township 2 North, Range 21 East, in the Town of Paris. GEM's point sits on a farm field beside Interstate 94, with a logistics warehouse to the north and an asphalt plant to the south, which matches the application.
qa.recommendation: Leave the point as it is and leave City as Somers, since the parcels sit in the Village of Somers growth area. The EIA point is about 870 meters to the west and is less accurate.
qa.note: Open https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=572462 and search for 'The Proposed Site is located in Section 13'. It says the Proposed Project Area consists of three parcels, and that 'Parcel 134-0101 is located in the Village of Somers Growth Area', while the other two sit in the City of Kenosha Growth Area. It also says the site is 'adjacent to an asphalt manufacturing plant, a logistics warehouse, and U.S. Interstate 41 / U.S. Interstate 94'. I looked at a satellite picture of GEM's point at 42.63143, -87.95560 and saw all three features. The imagery date is unknown. The air permit application at https://apps.dnr.wi.gov/warp_ext/AM_DownloadObject.aspx?id=1252907 is for the Alternative Site near Union Grove, which the Commission did not choose. The Commission minutes at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=615912 say it 'approved the applicant's proposed site and route'. The Commission page says Town of Paris, which is the township.
